title: The String Test

paragraphs.text: For many years, tool use was considered a hallmark of human intelligence. That view began to change as scientists observed members of the crow family—crows, ravens, and rooks—solving problems that required planning rather than simple trial and error. To study this ability in a controlled way, researchers developed a series of “string tests,” in which a small basket of food was attached to the end of a string and placed just out of reach.

In a basic version, the string hung from a perch near the bird. To get the reward, the bird had to pull the string up, pin it with a foot, and repeat this sequence several times until the basket reached the perch. Many corvids succeeded on their first try, suggesting they understood the connection between their actions and the rising basket. In more complex variants, two or more strings were presented, but only one was connected to the food. Birds that inspected the layout before acting were more likely to choose the correct string.

Similar problem-solving has been reported in other species. New Caledonian crows have dropped stones into tubes of water to raise floating food, while Eurasian jays and even some pigeons have performed simplified versions of the string task after brief exposure. These findings indicate that sophisticated problem-solving may be more widespread in birds than previously assumed.

基本的なバージョンでは、紐は止まり木のそばに垂れ下がっています。餌を手に入れるには、鳥は紐を引き上げ、足で押さえ、その動作を何度も繰り返して、かごを止まり木まで引き寄せる必要があります。多くのカラス科の鳥は、最初の試行でこれに成功しました。これは、自分の行動がかごを持ち上げることとつながっていることを理解していたことを示しています。より複雑な型では、2本以上の紐が提示され、しかし餌につながっているのは1本だけです。行動する前に配置を観察した鳥ほど、正しい紐を選ぶ可能性が高いことがわかりました。

title: The Detour Task

paragraphs.text: For decades, researchers have probed self-control in animals using a simple but revealing “detour task.” In the standard version, a piece of food is placed inside a clear cylinder that is open at both ends. The setup exploits a salient visual cue—the reward is plainly visible—while requiring the subject to inhibit a direct reach and instead approach from the side openings. Success on the first attempt is taken to indicate an ability to suppress impulse and map a short action sequence to an outcome.

When scientists compared species, they found notable differences. Pet dogs typically performed well, especially after a brief familiarization period, and often outscored hand-reared wolves. One interpretation is that experience with human-made objects gives dogs an advantage on this particular task. Corvids, such as crows and ravens, also excelled, frequently inspecting the apparatus before acting, whereas some pigeons persisted in pecking at the barrier. These contrasts suggest that both prior experience and species-typical strategies shape performance.

Related studies hint that such control is not confined to mammals and birds. In a separate delay-of-gratification paradigm, cuttlefish waited longer for a preferred reward when an immediate but less valuable option was available. Although the methods differ, the pattern strengthens a broader claim: forms of inhibitory control may be more widespread in the animal kingdom than once assumed.

title: The Clear Box Task

paragraphs.text: Scientists often study self-control in animals with a simple “clear box task.” A small piece of food is placed inside a transparent box that has doors on the sides. The food can be seen through the front wall, but it cannot be reached from there. To get the reward, the animal must resist the urge to touch the food directly and walk to a side door instead. Succeeding on the first try suggests that the animal can stop a quick reaction and choose a better route.

When researchers tested different species, they noticed some patterns. Pet dogs usually did well, especially after a short practice round, and in many studies they scored higher than wolves that were raised by humans. One possible reason is that dogs live with people and often deal with boxes, doors, and other everyday objects. Crows and ravens also did well. They often looked around the box before moving, while some pigeons kept pecking at the front wall even though it never worked.

Other studies point to the same idea. In a waiting test, cuttlefish sometimes passed up a small treat so they could get a better one later. The method is not the same as the clear box, but the lesson is similar: some form of self-control may be common in many kinds of animals.

title: The Abundance Trap

paragraphs.text: Modern media platforms promise limitless choice, yet many users report feeling less satisfied the longer they browse. This pattern fits a broader paradox: as the abundance of options rises, so does decision fatigue—the mental drain that comes from evaluating near-endless possibilities. While variety can match niche tastes, it also shifts attention from “good enough” choices to the fear of missing a slightly better one. Consequently, the pleasure of discovering content is crowded out by the pressure to optimize every selection.

Empirical work supports this tension. In one study, participants were asked to pick a movie to watch that evening. When offered 30 trailers, they sampled more but finished fewer films and rated their experience lower than a group given a curated set of 8. The limited menu reduced search costs and the fear of choosing poorly, making the decision feel easier and the outcome more enjoyable. Similarly, users who accepted platform-generated default playlists—assembled from prior viewing—were more likely to complete what they started than users who faced the full catalog.

The paradox also varies across cultures. In individualistic settings, personal choice is strongly valued; thus, the burden of choosing among countless options can weigh heavily. By contrast, in more collectivist environments, people often prefer guided recommendations from trusted sources, and they tend to report greater satisfaction when platforms filter the catalog for them. Understanding these differences helps services design options that support well-being rather than erode it.

title: The Metrics Paradox

paragraphs.text: Digital learning platforms promise that more feedback will drive better outcomes. Yet many learners report the opposite: as progress bars, streaks, badges, and percentile ranks multiply, motivation slips. This tension reflects a broader paradox—abundant metrics amplify self-monitoring and comparison, which can drain attention from the task itself. While fine-grained numbers seem informative, they also nudge users to optimize every micro-decision, increasing second-guessing and reducing satisfaction with perfectly adequate work.

Evidence supports this trade-off. In one study, students completed the same video lesson but saw different dashboards. One group viewed a granular display—minute-by-minute accuracy, speed, and rank; another saw a condensed summary with one progress bar and a short coach note. Learners using the condensed dashboard finished more lessons and rated the experience higher. Researchers argued that aggregation lowers “search costs” in decision-making and reduces fear of choosing the “wrong” study tactic. Similarly, participants who accepted platform-recommended study paths completed more modules than those browsing all options.

Cultural context also matters. In individualistic settings, achievement is often framed as personal optimization, so dense metrics can intensify pressure and self-comparison. By contrast, in more collectivist environments, learners frequently prefer guided routes or team-level feedback and report greater contentment when platforms filter information on their behalf. Recognizing these differences allows designers to present feedback that supports persistence rather than undermines it.

デジタル学習プラットフォームは、「より多くのフィードバックが、より良い成果につながる」と約束します。しかし実際には、多くの学習者がその逆を感じています。進捗バー、連続日数（ストリーク）、バッジ、偏差順位といった指標が増えるほど、やる気が下がってしまうというのです。この緊張は、より大きな逆説を示しています。すなわち、過剰な指標（abundant metrics）は自己監視や他者との比較を強め、学習そのものから注意を奪ってしまうということです。細かい数値は一見役に立つように見えますが、「すべてを最適化しなければならない」という意識を引き起こし、迷いや自信の低下を生み、十分良い出来でも満足できなくなります。
このトレードオフは研究でも確認されています。ある研究では、学生に同じビデオ授業を視聴してもらい、異なるダッシュボードを見せました。一方のグループには、1分ごとの正答率、速度、順位といった細分化された（granular）表示が示され、もう一方には、進捗バー1つと短いコーチコメントだけの簡潔な画面を見せました。すると、簡潔なダッシュボードを使った学習者の方が、より多くのレッスンを完了し、体験の満足度も高かったのです。研究者は、「情報をまとめることで、学習中の判断にかかる負担（search costs）が減り、間違った勉強法を選んでしまう不安が弱まった」と説明しました。また、プラットフォームが推奨する学習ルートに従った学習者は、全ての学習コンテンツから自分で選んだ学習者よりも、多くのモジュールを完了しました。
文化的な背景も影響します。個人主義的な文化では、成果は「自分自身の最適化」として捉えられがちなので、細かすぎる指標はプレッシャーや自己比較をさらに強めます。一方、より集団主義的な文化では、ガイドされた学習ルートやチーム単位のフィードバックが好まれ、情報をプラットフォーム側が整理してくれる方が満足度が高くなることがよくあります。こうした文化差を理解することで、学習者の継続を支える、より適切なフィードバック設計が可能になります。

title: The Filter Effect

paragraphs.text: Many services now offer thousands of items, yet users often enjoy the experience more when they see less. The puzzle is straightforward: greater abundance raises the chance of a perfect match, but it also increases mental load. People spend longer comparing options, second-guess themselves, and feel they should keep searching. Platforms therefore present a streamlined view—small, rotating sets or a default bundle—so the choice feels manageable rather than overwhelming.

Evidence backs this approach. In one field study, shoppers browsing an online market received either a full catalog or a pre-filtered list based on their stated preferences. Those seeing the filtered set sampled fewer items, decided faster, and—crucially—reported higher satisfaction with what they bought. Follow-up data showed that the curated list also reduced “switching”: users were less likely to abandon carts or reopen comparisons after checkout. The result did not mean fewer good matches; instead, it reduced the feeling that a slightly better option was always one more click away.

Cultural context matters. In more individualistic settings, people value personal agency and may resist heavy-handed limits, but they still benefit when filters are transparent and easy to adjust. In more collectivist environments, guidance from trusted sources is welcomed, and users often prefer systems that actively narrow the field. Designing filters with these tendencies in mind can protect well-being while keeping real choice intact.

title: The Shortlist Approach

paragraphs.text: Many apps and websites now show hundreds of items, but users often enjoy the process more when they see fewer. The reason is simple: more choices raise the chance of a perfect match, yet they also create mental workload. People compare for longer, switch between pages, and worry that a slightly better option is still out there. To help, some platforms present a simplified view—a small shortlist or a default set—so the decision feels clear and manageable.

A field test on a food-delivery app illustrates this effect. New users were randomly shown either the full menu of about 40 dishes or a shortlist of 6 based on their stated likes. Those who saw the shortlist decided faster, went back and forth less, and rated their meal higher the next day. Importantly, the match quality did not drop: the chosen dishes still fit the users’ preferences. The shortlist reduced the feeling of “maybe there’s something better,” which often leads to hesitation and late changes.

Culture shapes how filters should work. In more individualistic settings, people want control, so they respond well when the shortlist is easy to edit or turn off. In more collectivist settings, many users prefer guidance from trusted sources, such as store “recommended” labels or staff picks. Designing filters with these patterns in mind can protect well-being while keeping real choice.

title: Daily Life - Notice 2

paragraphs.text:
Read a notice.
MetroLink City
Tap & Go — move to contactless fares.
Skip the ticket lines and keep your balance safe. Register your contactless card to see your recent trips, set up auto top-ups, and replace a lost card without losing money.
To begin, sign in to your MetroLink account on the website, open Cards & Payments, and update your delivery and security preferences anytime.

translationJa:
タップ＆ゴー — 運賃をキャッシュレスに。
券売機の列に並ぶ必要はありません。残高も安全に管理できます。コンタクトレスカードを登録すると、最近の乗車履歴を確認したり、自動チャージを設定したり、カードを紛失した際に残高を失わずに再発行できます。
始めるには、MetroLinkのウェブサイトでアカウントにサインインし、「カード＆支払い」を開いてください。配達方法やセキュリティ設定はいつでも変更できます。

questions.prompt: Who most likely posted this notice?
options: A museum network
A public transit authority
A package delivery service
A cinema chain
questions.answer: A public transit authority
questions.explanation: 「contactless fares」「trips」などから、切符や運賃を扱う公共交通の掲示と推論。本文には “transit authority” とは書かれていないが、語彙手掛かりから判断。

questions.prompt: What is one advantage of registering the card?
options: You’ll receive paper tickets by mail each month.
You can recover the remaining balance if the card goes missing.
You’ll earn airline miles for every trip taken.
You can ride for free during weekends.
questions.answer: You can recover the remaining balance if the card goes missing.
questions.explanation: 本文の “replace a lost card without losing money” をパラフレーズ。登録すると紛失時に残高を保全できることが利点。A・C・Dはいずれも本文根拠なし。

title: Daily Life - Notice 3

paragraphs.text:
Read a notice.
Henderson Learning Commons
Group Spaces & Quiet Study Update
Need a place to work with classmates? Reserve a group room through the campus portal under Spaces & Bookings. Please arrive with your student ID and check in at the front counter. If no one from your group appears within 10 minutes after the start time, the room will be released for other students.
Quiet zones are located on the upper floor; phones must be on silent. Study areas stay open until midnight during exam week.

translationJa:
グループスペース & 静かな学習エリアについてのお知らせ
クラスメートと一緒に作業する場所が必要ですか？キャンパスポータルの 「スペース & 予約」 からグループルームを予約できます。来館の際は学生証を持参し、受付でチェックインしてください。開始時刻から10分以内にグループの誰も来ない場合、その部屋は他の学生に開放されます。
静かな学習ゾーンは上階にあります。携帯電話はマナーモードに設定してください。試験期間中は学習エリアが深夜まで開放されています。

questions.prompt: Which campus unit most likely posted this notice?
options: The athletics department
The student health center
The campus library service
The dining hall
questions.answer: The campus library service
questions.explanation: “Spaces & Bookings”（自習室予約）、“Quiet zones”（静粛エリア）、“upper floor” などの手掛かりから図書館サービスが発信者と推論できる（本文に “library” の語は未出）。

questions.prompt: What happens if a group doesn’t show up soon after the booking begins?
options: The reservation is automatically extended
The space becomes available to others
A late fee is added to the account
The booking is moved to the next day
questions.answer: The space becomes available to others
questions.explanation: “If no one … within 10 minutes … the room will be released for other students” とあるため、他の利用者に開放が正答。A・C・Dは本文根拠なし。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 1

paragraphs.text: Campus Career Center

translationJa:
キャンパス・キャリアセンター
今夏のインターンやアルバイトを探していますか？
「スプリング・キャリア・ポップアップ」 が 今週の水曜日 11:30〜14:00、学生会館ロビー で開催されます。
テック、デザイン、教育、非営利団体など 35社が参加
履歴書を10部 持参してください（その場での履歴書チェックも可能）
30秒の自己紹介を試せる 「ピッチ練習」ブース あり
先着150名 にネットワーキングランチチケットを配布
服装は スマートカジュアル でOK。リュックも可。
今夜中にオンライン登録 をすると、企業配置マップが事前に受け取れ、チェックインの列をスキップできます。
参加できない場合は、当日のリクルーターのアドバイスをストーリーでチェックしてください。
お待ちしています！

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the post?
options: To review last year’s outcomes of the career fair
To announce and encourage attendance at a recruiting event
To explain how to write a strong résumé from scratch
To compare salaries across industries for summer jobs
questions.answer: To announce and encourage attendance at a recruiting event
questions.explanation: 投稿全体は「今週水曜のキャリアイベントに来てね」という告知＋参加促進。Aは過去の振り返り、C・Dはトピックが本文の目的とずれ。

questions.prompt: According to the post, what is one advantage of registering the night before?
options: You can book one-on-one interviews in advance.
You will receive a floor layout and avoid the entry queue.
You will be guaranteed a lunch ticket.
You can access premium workshops after the event.
questions.answer: You will receive a floor layout and avoid the entry queue.
questions.explanation: “Register online tonight to receive the employer map and skip the check-in line.” と明記。A・Dは未記載、Cは「先着150名」なので登録=保証ではない。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the expected dress code?
options: Formal business suits are required for entry.
Athletic wear is preferred due to long lines.
Neat everyday clothing is acceptable.
Students must store bags off-site.
questions.answer: Neat everyday clothing is acceptable.
questions.explanation: “Dress is smart casual—backpacks welcome.”＝きれいめカジュアル可。Aは要求レベルが過剰、Bは根拠なし、Dは「バックパック可」なので逆。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 2

paragraphs.text: Riverstone Community Gym

translationJa:
リバーストーン・コミュニティジム
そろそろ運動習慣に戻りたいと考えていますか？
リバーストーンでは、今週（月〜日）6:00〜22:00の期間中、無料体験ウィークを開催します。新規の方は、朝ヨガ、夕方のHIIT、初心者向けのやさしいモビリティクラスなど、どのクラスでも無料で参加できます。
朝8:00より前に来館された方には、スムージーバーでプロテインサンプルを無料提供。また、館内には終日トレーナーが常駐しており、フォームチェックなどの簡単なアドバイスが受けられます。
ロッカーとタオルは無料貸し出し。予約は不要ですが、土曜日のスピンクラスのみ要予約（毎回すぐに満席になります）。
18:00以降は駐車場が混み合うため、Elm駅から徒歩3分（Pine Street沿い）で来館されることをおすすめします。
初めての方は、受付で身分証をお持ちください。
来館にまだ迷っている方は、インスタのストーリーでクラスの様子や初心者向けのヒントもご覧いただけます。
今週、お待ちしています！

questions.prompt: Why was this message posted?
options: To publish a critique of nearby fitness centers
To promote a weeklong open-access period and nudge newcomers to attend
To set out compulsory safety codes for intense training
To recruit part-time smoothie-bar staff
questions.answer: To promote a weeklong open-access period and nudge newcomers to attend
questions.explanation: ポストは「Free Trial Week」「try any class without charge」「See you this week!」と、無料体験週間への参加を呼びかける内容。= “週にわたる自由参加期間を案内して来場を促す”

questions.prompt: What must a first-time guest present to activate a visitor pass?
options: A printed liability waiver
Cash to cover towel use
Proof of identity with a photograph
A document confirming current residence
questions.answer: Proof of identity with a photograph
questions.explanation: 「First-time guests should bring a photo ID to activate the visitor pass.」= 初来館者は写真付き身分証が必要。

questions.prompt: What is implied about the Saturday spin class?
options: It is the only session that requires payment
Places tend to be gone unless you book ahead
It runs only at daybreak
It is cancelled whenever evening parking is crowded
questions.answer: Places tend to be gone unless you book ahead
questions.explanation: 「no reservation is required except for the Saturday spin class, which fills quickly」= 土曜スピンは満員になりやすい→事前予約が実質必要。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット1
passageTitle: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット1

paragraphs.text: Harborlight Indie Cinema

translationJa:
ハーバーライト・インディー・シネマ
週の真ん中に、ちょっと深く考えさせられる作品はいかがですか？
今週の水曜日 19:30〜、ドキュメンタリー・ナイトを開催します。
今回は、海洋保全と小さな町のジャーナリズムをテーマにした、受賞歴のある短編ドキュメンタリーを上映します。
開場は19:00、座席は先着順です。
メンバーの方は、上映前にカウンターで無料のティーをお受け取りいただけます。
上映終了後には、監督2名による15分のQ&Aを予定しています。
*チケット料金は「お気持ち制」**で、当日ボックスオフィスにてお支払いください。
もし満席となった場合は、学生証提示の方が優先入場となります。
夜遅くまでいられない方のために、
翌朝、ストーリーにハイライト映像を投稿します。

questions.prompt: What is the post mainly trying to do?
options: Review last month’s film festival results
Invite people to attend a midweek nonfiction screening
Explain how to apply for a directing grant
Compare documentary and fiction box office trends
questions.answer: Invite people to attend a midweek nonfiction screening
questions.explanation: 「Documentary Night」「this Wednesday 7:30」「pay-what-you-can」など、参加を促す告知。

questions.prompt: According to the post, what benefit do members receive?
options: Reserved seats in the front row
A complimentary hot drink at the venue
Discounted parking near the cinema
Early access to the next month’s schedule
questions.answer: A complimentary hot drink at the venue
questions.explanation: 「members can pick up a free tea at the counter」＝会員の特典。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about entry if many people show up?
options: Only directors may enter after 7:30 p.m.
Students with ID are admitted before others.
Everyone must buy a full-price ticket online.
No one will be allowed to stand in the aisles.
questions.answer: Students with ID are admitted before others.
questions.explanation: 「student IDs get priority entry if we hit capacity」＝混雑時は学生優先。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット2
passageTitle: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット2

paragraphs.text: Maple Street Animal Rescue

translationJa:
メイプルストリート動物レスキュー
里親に興味はあるけど、いきなりは不安……という方にぴったりの**「フォスター・ウィークエンド」を開催します。土曜日の10:00〜13:00の間に犬または猫を受け取り、日曜の夕方まで一緒に過ごしてください。その後、戻ってきた際に写真と様子のメモ**をいただければ、動物たちと新しい家族とのよりよいマッチングに役立てることができます。
フード、移動用クレート、24時間対応のホットラインは当団体がご用意します。
予約なしの来訪でも大丈夫ですが、事前にオンラインフォームを記入していただくと受け渡しがスムーズです。
他のペットがいるご家庭でも、ワクチン接種が済んでいれば参加OKです。
今回はホストできない方も、お散歩ボランティアに参加できます（予約不要）。

questions.prompt: What is the chief aim of the message?
options: To promote a short-term home-care trial for animals
To announce permanent closures at the shelter
To recruit paid weekend staff for the clinic
To advertise a pet-supply sale
questions.answer: To promote a short-term home-care trial for animals
questions.explanation: 「Foster Weekend… try it」「土日で短期お試し」＝短期預かりの体験を促進。

questions.prompt: What is one convenience offered to participants?
options: Free grooming at drop-off
A loaner carrier and food included
House-checking by staff beforehand
A stipend for transportation
questions.answer: A loaner carrier and food included
questions.explanation: 「We provide food and a travel crate and a hotline」＝参加者の負担軽減。

questions.prompt: What is implied about the online form?
options: It guarantees a specific breed.
It is mandatory for all volunteers.
It reduces waiting time on arrival.
It enrolls participants in weekly shifts.
questions.answer: It reduces waiting time on arrival.
questions.explanation: 「Walk-ins are fine, but completing the online form tonight speeds up pickup」＝到着時の手続き短縮。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット3
passageTitle: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット3

paragraphs.text: Riverview City Museum

translationJa:
リバービュー市立博物館
今週日曜日は、毎月のコミュニティプログラムの一環として終日入館無料です。
新しい「河川交易」展は10:00にオープンします。
またファミリースタジオでは、毎時ちょうどから短いアートアクティビティを行います。
ベビーカーでの来館も歓迎ですが、ロビーは昼食後に混雑しやすいため、
ゆっくり見たい場合は11:00より前のご来館がおすすめです。
会員の方はオーディオガイドを無料で貸出、
非会員の方も受付でレンタルできます。
カフェは営業時間を18:00まで延長します。
来館できない方向けには、おうちで楽しめる子ども向け制作アイデアをストーリーで公開します。

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the post?
options: To seek donations for a renovation
To encourage attendance on a no-fee day
To recruit artists for a residency
To report research findings about river trade
questions.answer: To encourage attendance on a no-fee day
questions.explanation: 「admission is free all day」「monthly community program」＝無料日への来館促進。

questions.prompt: What advice does the post give to avoid crowds?
options: Visit before late morning.
Use the side entrance.
Skip the lobby and go to the café.
Reserve timed tickets online.
questions.answer: Visit before late morning.
questions.explanation: 「the lobby gets crowded after lunch; … come before 11」＝早い時間帯を推奨。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about audio guides?
options: They are unavailable to visitors with strollers.
They are complimentary for everyone.
They are only in foreign languages.
Members pay nothing; others can rent them.
questions.answer: Members pay nothing; others can rent them.
questions.explanation: 「Members can check out audio guides at no charge; non-members may rent」＝会員無料、非会員は有料レンタル。

title: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット4
passageTitle: Daily Life - Social Post 3-6 セット4

paragraphs.text: Canal Yard Food Trucks

translationJa:
キャナルヤード・フードトラック
今週金曜日の17:00〜21:00、新しい照明と座席配置のテストを兼ねてソフトオープンを行います。
日替わりのフードトラックが、タコス、ヴィーガンボウル、デザートポップを提供します。現在は機材調整中のため、メニューは通常より少なめです。
カード・モバイル決済OK。
早めに来ると、ヒーター付きのパティオ席を確保できることが多いです。
18:00以降は周辺の路上駐車が混み合うため、
近隣の方はBirch駅から徒歩約4分で歩いて来られることが多いです。
もし風が強くなった場合は、ストーリーでお知らせし、一部のトラックを屋根付きエリアへ移動します。

questions.prompt: What is the principal goal of the announcement?
options: To hire cooks for the new season
To invite the public to a limited-scale trial evening
To collect feedback on dessert recipes online only
To announce a price increase for all vendors
questions.answer: To invite the public to a limited-scale trial evening
questions.explanation: 「soft opening… test the new lighting and seating」＝限定規模の試運転に招待。

questions.prompt: What is suggested about seating?
options: Only VIPs can use patio tables.
Seats require a reservation fee.
Arriving early improves your chance of getting a spot.
Indoor dining is the only option in any weather.
questions.answer: Arriving early improves your chance of getting a spot.
questions.explanation: 「early birds often land patio tables」＝早く来ると座れる確率↑。

questions.prompt: What arrangement is implied for transportation?
options: Free valet service begins at 6.
A shuttle runs every four minutes.
Most locals walk from a nearby transit stop due to tight parking.
Bicycle parking is prohibited near the venue.
questions.answer: Most locals walk from a nearby transit stop due to tight parking.
questions.explanation: 「Street parking is scarce after 6, so neighbors usually walk from Birch Station」＝駐車難→最寄り駅から徒歩が一般的。
